text: An archive or purge record carries the archive decision code from LOV-DECISION in force, a final call from the final-call list in force, no rule ID (no Drools rule decides an archive action), the rule version in force and the run reference in inputsRef, and the data product, table, counts archived and kept, hold report reference and archive location in actions and outcome.
why: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 gives the columns and no source names the values, and the record must still be assertable and groupable by run.
read: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 DF-DEC-003, -004, -005, -008, -009, -012, -014 and -015; T3.2; FSD P7 v3 AC-EXC-P7-002-01 and AC-EXC-P7-002-05; RWB-E1-017 section 4 step 9 and section 12.
confirm: Solution architect with the P7 business analyst and the reference-data owner
impact: Medium: the placement is a contract choice made once, and the values become reference rows, so a new code is a data change and no scenario changes.

text: MSG-P7-009 is the carrier of both refusals of this slice — a record whose code is outside LOV-DECISION or lacks ruleVersion or inputsRef, and a record that names a table of rwb_decision — and it carries the legacy AC8 check name character for character; the not-found answer, the chain-break report and the collection gap alert keep a placeholder for id and text.
why: The FSD names MSG-P7-009 without a text and allocates no id to the other three outcomes, and the legacy check name is already asserted by the P1 and P5 slices.
read: FSD P7 v3 A2.1.3.1, A2.2.3.1 and A2.2.4.3; RWB-E1-017 sections 5 and 14 (MSG-P1-002 and the AC8 check name).
confirm: Business analyst, P7, with the message and localisation owners
impact: Low: no behaviour changes; only the wording and the ids of four outcomes are deferred.

text: JOB-14 runs daily at 02:00 Asia/Bangkok on queue rwb-decision as a Temporal Schedule that starts DecisionChainCheckWorkflow, reads the chain in pages of 5000 and allows one run at a time with a catch-up window; when the feature flag is off the collection pauses, the check does not run and the two reads answer as of the last committed entry, never as a complete answer.
why: Architecture v5 slide 44 fixes the 02:00 time and the daily cadence and no source fixes the timezone, the page size, the overlap and catch-up policy, the property names or the flag-off answer.
read: Architecture v5 slide 44 and slide 28 through the P7 context pack; TSD P7 v2 NFR-035; FSD P7 v3 AC-BG-P7-001-01; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-10.
confirm: Solution architect with the workflow platform owner and the platform administrator
impact: Low: the check is daily either way and the values are configuration, so a later change touches no scenario.

text: This story is the secondary P7 slice of RWB-E1-017: it owns no legacy acceptance criterion, its fragment carries an empty acs list, its eight criteria are new and test only the ledger deliverable, and the metadata rows stay exactly as the Work Package fixes them, with Depends on (build) empty and RWB-P1-E1017-CON as the only contract dependency, while the five platform H rows of the pattern table, the rwb-case reference-data contract and the rwb-access authorise contract are named in sections 3, 12.2, 12.8 and 13 and built against their fakes from Day 1.
why: Only step D1 may change the plan, and the patterns the Work Package fixes add rows the story line does not carry; naming them where they are used keeps the metadata exact and the dependency visible.
read: Work Package B2-P7-008 story line; Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R5.7 rules 2 and 8; P7 context pack ownership rows.
confirm: Solution architect with the delivery lead and the owners of the four platform contracts
impact: No behaviour change; ready to start stays Day 1 because every H is a wave 0 platform contract and a C never blocks.

text: The story names the database login only as 'the rwb-decision login (DP-02)' and leaves the name to the ACE team, because no source gives it.
why: Template and Rules R4 and DP-02 fix one login per service and name none of them, and a story may not invent a credential name.
read: Template and Rules v1 R4 and R5.5 DP-02; P7 context pack naming rules.
impact: Low: the login is provisioned with the schema in wave 1 and nothing else depends on the spelling.

text: The story file at the fixed path is written by this Work Package from the legacy story and the P7 module sources, replacing the partial artefact of the superseded Work Package B-P7-05, whose fourteen citations resolved to no register row; the substance of that artefact — the one-record-per-action rule, the exclusion of every table of rwb_decision, the fail-closed write, the 02:00 chain check and the two reads — is carried forward, and no orphan citation is left in the tree.
why: Root rule 1 forbids editing an existing file and the Work Package fixes this exact path as the deliverable, so the two rules meet; the earlier artefact was an abandoned partial with no fragment, no register rows and no edit log, and root rule 1 also forbids writing a path outside the Write only block, which a v2 copy would be.
read: Work Package B2-P7-008 Write only list; _work/msr/status.json (B-P7-05 SUPERSEDED); _work/msr/fragments and _work/msr/gaps (no row of the earlier Work Package).
applied_in: Whole story file, _work/msr/fragments/RWB-P7-E1017-APP.json and the edit log
confirm: Delivery lead, with the traceability owner at the stage gate
impact: The tree holds one coherent story with resolved citations and a fragment; the version history of the abandoned partial is recorded in this row and in the edit log instead of in a second file.

why: The Work Package fixes acs empty and the ten legacy test cases, and Template and Rules R7.2 s16 requires the Level column with values the legacy story does not use.

impact: Low: the legacy criteria stay proved by RWB-P1-E1017-APP, RWB-P5-E1017-APP and RWB-ITG-E1017-ITG, and no test case ID is added or dropped.

text: The retention values used in the scenarios stay the legacy values — rule version RET-2026.11, 24 months, product DP05 table interaction on occurred_at, and the run date Sunday 2026-12-06 — because the bank retention schedule is still open under DL26 and a story may not set a period.
why: RWB-E1-017 states the period as assumed until Compliance supplies the schedule, and the Decision Log DL26 keeps the item open.
read: RWB-E1-017 sections 3 and 7 (assumed until Compliance supplies the bank schedule; DL26); Decision Log DL26.
confirm: Compliance and PDPA officer, with the data steward
